title: Engineering aptamer dimers (apdimers) for optimization of synthetic riboswitches.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplement (1.78 MB) and extracted all 7 pages of the only data file, gkag702_supplemental_file.pdf. It contains Supplementary Table 1 (RNA sequences of 16 named aptamer/riboswitch constructs, as free text in a PDF table, no measurements), three figure legends, and a reference list. I also searched the whole open-access full text for 'library', 'screen', 'deep sequencing', 'GEO', 'Zenodo' and 'source data': no repository accession, no deposited numeric table, no Excel/CSV file anywhere.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The performance numbers themselves (fold change up to ~1000x, background expression ~5-8%, EC50 and Hill coefficient from the dose-response fits, mouse bioluminescence results) come only from the figures and prose; I read them in the text and could not open them as data because no numeric file exists.

a1_downloadable.note: The one supplementary file downloads freely and I opened it. But it is a 7-page PDF of sequences and figure legends, not a dataset; there is no repository deposit at all.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The thing a model would predict (switching fold change, OFF-state background, EC50) exists nowhere as a column. It would have to be reconstructed by reading values off bar charts in Figures 2-8, which is label construction by eye.

a3_inputs_present.note: The RNA sequences are present as literal text for all 16 constructs, so inputs would not need accession lookups; they would need copy-pasting out of a PDF table.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL for modelling purposes. Figure legends state 'relative luciferase activity' normalized to a psiCHECK control and 'fold change', but no units column exists because no table exists; normalization differs between splicing and aptazyme reporter layouts.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL, decisively. I counted exactly 16 named constructs in Supplementary Table 1 (5 Tet_splice/apdimer, 1 TetK19 benchmark, 4 Tet_HHR series, 6 Theo_splice series). The checklist floor is ~1,500 rows, or ~400 for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small; size was never the problem.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable: there is no machine-readable file whose row count could be compared to the paper, so the check cannot be performed either way.

a8_label_provenance.note: Provenance is clean in principle: dual-luciferase assays in transfected HeLa cells, three biological replicates, plus mouse AAV bioluminescence. Not a model output and not computable from the sequence. The problem is quantity and format, not circularity.

backbone.name: RNA-FM or a secondary-structure feature set would have been the natural fit for short RNA regulators
backbone.hardware: CPU only would suffice for 16 sequences, which is the point: 16 examples cannot train or evaluate any head
backbone.licence: Not assessed; project died at Part A

integration.partner_dataset: Strobel et al. 2020, Nature Communications 11:714, a barcode-free amplicon-sequencing screen of synthetic riboswitches in human cells (cited as reference 26 by this paper) would be the real dataset to go after
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Can sequence-based models predict the ON/OFF dynamic range of a synthetic riboswitch well enough to replace high-throughput screening, and do the rational apdimer design rules in this paper fall out of such a model?

controls.positive_control: Would have been the published TetK19 benchmark switch, whose performance is known from Beilstein et al. 2015; but with 16 rows there is nothing to control.
controls.negative_control: Catalytically inactive aptazyme constructs are present in the mouse experiment, a genuine negative, but only as figure panels.
controls.external_validation: None in this paper; the Strobel 2020 screen would have to supply it.

honest_claim_h3: No honest model claim is possible: with 16 rationally designed constructs measured in one lab on one reporter, any model would be describing this paper's design intuition, not predicting riboswitch performance.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a synthetic RNA switch's sequence to predict how strongly a drug turns the attached gene on.
plain_idea.train_on: The RNA sequence of each engineered riboswitch construct. I verified there are 16 such sequences in this paper, printed in a PDF table.
plain_idea.predict: How many fold gene expression rises when the small-molecule drug (tetracycline or theophylline) is added, and how much expression leaks in the off state. The true answer comes from a dual-luciferase assay in human HeLa cells, three biological replicates, reported in this paper only as bar charts.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Gene-therapy groups want a drug-controlled on/off switch for an AAV-delivered transgene and currently find good ones by screening thousands of variants in the lab; a sequence-to-performance model would skip that. This paper is far too small to build one.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict riboswitch dynamic range and off-state background from construct sequence, with RNA-FM embeddings or folding-energy features plus a small head. The idea is sound but this paper supplies 16 labelled constructs in a PDF, so the correct target is a high-throughput screen such as Strobel et al. 2020 (Nature Communications 11:714, amplicon sequencing of synthetic riboswitch libraries in human cells), which this paper itself cites as the costly alternative to its rational approach.

effort.compute_note: Only the PDF size was measured. No training-time estimate is meaningful because there are 16 examples and no numeric labels.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the supplement: unzipping one 1.78 MB archive and reading a 7-page PDF showed 16 construct sequences and zero numeric measurement tables. That took one tool call and kills the project.

verdict_reason: Fails A5, A2 and A4. The entire dataset is 16 rationally designed riboswitch sequences in a PDF table; the performance values (fold change, background, EC50) exist only as bar charts and prose, so the label would have to be eyeballed off figures. Nothing is deposited in any repository. Excellent synthetic-biology paper, not a machine-learning dataset; the companion idea should be pursued against a published high-throughput riboswitch screen instead.
